original_test_intent: Inject a transient DRAM command/address parity error into each approved memory-controller target with CAP enabled, then prove Cscript success, corrected platform handling, the specified BMC/UEFI attribution and absence of fault-light assertion while the system remains operational.
original_method: A qualified FAE/operator applies the approved BIOS controls, confirms the current socket/controller/channel map and CAP state, substitutes a vendor-valid fully named command for the malformed source call, performs one bounded injection per approved coverage target, correlates Cscript and platform evidence, restores settings and verifies health.
manual_activity: The operator/FAE must enable approved debug/CAP settings, map each controller target, provide the valid Cscript call, execute the bounded injection and restore settings. The agent must not silently repair or run the malformed source command.
required_inputs: Platform socket/memory-controller/channel/DIMM topology and controller 1~N coverage matrix
Approved Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash, namespace and valid injectCMDParity signature
Authoritative CAP field meaning and required pre-state
Expected transient/correctable severity, Cscript success string and BMC/UEFI/indicator oracle
Dedicated-SUT approval, timeout, backup, recovery and BIOS restoration plan
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent console, backup and qualified FAE approval
Preserve baseline CAP/register/log state; do not clear historical evidence merely for a baseline
Use only an owner-approved syntactically valid fully resolved target call
Perform one bounded target injection at a time and stop on wrong severity, error storm, crash, data concern or failed resume
No automatic retry; restore debug/CAP settings and verify normal operation
agent_execution_scope: Validate supplied target map and CAP/evidence captures; collect read-only Cscript, Windows, BMC, UEFI and health evidence
Do not correct the command by inference, select targets, change BIOS/CAP, inject, reset/retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve exact Cscript interface and controller coverage
Define CAP semantics and correctable transient-parity oracle
Resolve Windows evidence source, BMC no-slot versus UEFI slot behavior and indicator applicability

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The post-event grep is insufficient and weakens SSH trust; it does not validate CAP, the target, Cscript success, exact severity, UEFI/indicator state or normal operation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not execute `ei.injectCMDParity(socket, hbm=-1, mc, channel)`: positional arguments after `hbm=-1` are invalid Python-like syntax. Use only the FAE-approved namespace and fully named target form for this package/version.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CAP on, memory-controller 1~N, transient parity purpose and 20/5-minute estimates are preserved; no namespace, target values or HBM semantics are invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture CAP and relevant parity/status registers, resolve one target from the approved topology, run one fully named vendor command, time-correlate Cscript success with Windows/WHEA, BMC and UEFI evidence, verify indicators remain off and system health remains normal, then restore/diff settings.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the malformed call, target coverage, severity and normal-operation evidence executable and measurable without rewriting the Master row.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A parity keyword does not prove the intended controller was injected, CAP handled a transient corrected event or the required no-slot/off-indicator behavior occurred.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong namespace or target may inject another controller or severity and can crash the SUT; debug settings also broaden the fault-injection surface.

project_override_considerations: The exact vendor call and controller/channel target are material parameters. The agent may not infer them from row 163 or treat a syntax failure as a DUT failure.
expected_evidence: Package version/hash, approved target map, pre/post BIOS and CAP state
Exact valid command plus complete Cscript output proving injection success
Time-correlated Windows/WHEA/parity evidence, BMC correctable no-slot record, applicable UEFI slot record and off-indicator evidence
Normal-operation health, restoration diff, unexpected-event check and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The literal call places positional `mc, channel` after keyword `hbm=-1` and is not executable as Python-like Cscript syntax. Controller 1~N lacks a map/count, parity severity is underspecified, Windows conflicts with dmesg, and optional/contrasting BMC no-slot versus UEFI slot evidence is not deterministic.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The transient command/address-parity purpose is identifiable. A valid package-specific signature, topology, CAP definition and oracle are obtainable prerequisites, so static review can complete while execution remains gated.

review_improvement: This review identifies a non-runnable source command and prevents either a guessed repair or a syntax error from being mistaken for DRAM-parity test evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Command/address parity injection is target-specific and package-version-specific. The source call cannot be executed literally because it uses positional arguments after a keyword argument. A similar historical row demonstrates that valid syntax and its namespace can differ, but it does not authorize copying that interface or target into this variant. CAP-on, the controller map, exact corrected severity and Cscript status/register evidence are necessary to distinguish the intended transient event from a generic memory error. Since an FAE can supply these inputs and a recovery plan, the correct classification is REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION rather than BLOCKED.
